column1: # Jawwid Chat WORKER environment-variable manifest. Owner: AI #7 (infrastructure).
# The machine-readable source of truth for the environment of the BACKGROUND
# WORKER (`node dist/worker.js`), which is a different process from the API and
# must not be given the API's environment. Consumed by
# scripts/infra/check-env.sh --component worker.
# Columns are exactly those of infra/env/manifest.tsv (tab-separated):
#   NAME     variable name
#   GROUP    documentation grouping
#   SECRET   yes = must come from the secret store, never from a tracked file
#   LOCAL    req | opt | forbid
#   STAGING  req | opt | forbid
#   PROD     req | opt | forbid   -- forbid = deployment is refused if present
# WHY THIS FILE EXISTS AT ALL
# infra/env/manifest.tsv declares itself to describe the API process, and its
# six columns have no axis on which to say "required for the worker, forbidden
# for the API". Both processes need that sentence said about the same variable
# in opposite directions, so the contract is two files rather than one column
# that cannot exist. Named as the fix in docs/recovery/PHASE-1-REPORT.md 11.5.
# THE INVERSION, AND WHY IT IS THE WHOLE POINT
#   API     DATABASE_URL          chat_app      NOBYPASSRLS  (required)
#           DATABASE_SERVICE_URL                             (FORBIDDEN)
#   worker  DATABASE_SERVICE_URL  chat_service  BYPASSRLS    (required)
#           DATABASE_URL                                     (FORBIDDEN)
# The worker acts for the SYSTEM: it drains the outbox and runs the deadline
# sweeps, and there is no actor whose context it could adopt. Connected as
# chat_app it still CLAIMS outbox rows -- that table carries a blanket policy --
# but every read it needs in order to route what it claimed returns nothing, so
# it marks each row published and delivers it to nobody, with no error anywhere.
# DATABASE_URL is therefore forbidden rather than merely unrequired: the runtime
# refuses to fall back (platform/database-role.ts), and a variable that cannot
# be present cannot be fallen back to.
# DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL is forbidden here for the same reason it is forbidden
# for the API: the owner/DDL credential belongs to CI, for the length of one
# migration step, and nowhere else.
# QUEUE_PREFIX MUST BE BYTE-IDENTICAL TO THE API'S. It namespaces the Redis
# pub/sub channel (infra/realtime/realtime-channel.ts), and pub/sub is global to
# the Redis SERVER rather than to the selected database. A mismatch is silent:
# the worker publishes to a channel no API instance is listening on, so events
# are "delivered" and nobody receives them. No gate can catch it -- the two
# values are supplied independently at deploy time -- so it is stated here.
# WHAT IS DELIBERATELY ABSENT, AND WHY
#   PORT, CORS_ALLOWED_ORIGINS   the worker starts no HTTP server and must not
#                                hold a port (worker.ts). PORT is omitted rather
#                                than forbidden because some platforms inject it
#                                into every component, and a gate that fails on
#                                the platform's own variable is a gate nobody
#                                trusts.
#   JWT_*                        read only inside auth methods the worker never
#                                calls.
#   LIVEKIT_*                    read with `?? ''`; never throw, never used here.
#   DATABASE_TRANSACTION_*       read inside PrismaService.runWithActor, whose
#                                only caller is the HTTP actor interceptor.
#   ATTACHMENT_MAX_BYTES_*       defaulted, and used by the API's attachment
#                                endpoints rather than by any worker path.
#   WORKER_CONCURRENCY           read by nothing. Despite the name it does not
#                                configure this process: the loop is sequential,
#                                and the only real concurrency control is the
#                                database-backed `broadcast.fanout_concurrency`.
#   FCM_PROJECT_ID               read by nothing; the project id comes from
#                                inside FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON.
#   LOG_LEVEL, REQUEST_TIMEOUT_MS, DATABASE_POOL_MAX,
#   DATABASE_STATEMENT_TIMEOUT_MS, JWT_REFRESH_TTL
#                                read by nothing. A new contract must not be
#                                born requiring values no code reads.
# WHY STORAGE IS REQUIRED FOR A PROCESS THAT UPLOADS NOTHING
# The worker builds the whole AppModule, so Nest constructs OBJECT_STORAGE
# whether or not the worker calls it. With the four S3 variables set it builds
# S3ObjectStorage; without them it builds the local signer, whose field
# initializer throws unless STORAGE_SIGNING_SECRET is at least 32 characters.
# Either way the worker does not start unless one of those branches is
# satisfied, so both are required here.
#NAME
NODE_ENV
APP_ENV
SHUTDOWN_GRACE_MS
DATABASE_SERVICE_URL
DATABASE_URL
DATABASE_MIGRATION_URL
REDIS_URL
QUEUE_PREFIX
OUTBOX_POLL_MS
OUTBOX_BATCH_SIZE
OUTBOX_IDLE_BACKOFF_MS
CALL_SWEEP_MS
STORAGE_ENDPOINT
STORAGE_REGION
STORAGE_BUCKET
STORAGE_ACCESS_KEY
STORAGE_SECRET_KEY
STORAGE_SIGNED_URL_TTL_SECONDS
STORAGE_SIGNING_SECRET
FCM_SERVICE_ACCOUNT_JSON
APNS_KEY_ID
APNS_TEAM_ID
APNS_BUNDLE_ID
APNS_PRIVATE_KEY
APNS_ENVIRONMENT
SENTRY_DSN
GIT_COMMIT
